title: Shortlist the solvers a model can go to

blocks.text: A freight company's planning service receives models from several teams and must send each to a solver that will answer the model as written. You decide from the model alone, before any solve.
Write `shortlist(model, need_duals=False)` in `shortlist.py`. It returns the solvers of `CANDIDATES` (GLOP, PDLP, HiGHS, SCIP, CP-SAT, in that order) that may take the model, keeping that order:

items: **GLOP and PDLP** solve LPs only: drop them if any variable is integer.
**CP-SAT** works over integers: drop it if any variable is continuous, since it would round that variable and still report `OPTIMAL`.
**Dual values** (`need_duals=True`) come only from GLOP, PDLP and HiGHS, and only for an LP: drop SCIP and CP-SAT, and if any variable is integer, no solver can give them, so return an empty list.

blocks.text:
from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

S = mathopt.SolverType
CANDIDATES = (S.GLOP, S.PDLP, S.HIGHS, S.GSCIP, S.CP_SAT)


def shortlist(model: mathopt.Model, need_duals: bool = False) -> list[mathopt.SolverType]:
    """The candidate solvers that answer this model as written, in CANDIDATES order."""
    # TODO: drop the solvers each rule of the statement rules out.
    return list(CANDIDATES)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = mathopt.Model()
    model.add_binary_variable(name="ship")
    model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=40, name="tons")
    print([s.name for s in shortlist(model)])

cases.says: a model with only continuous variables is shortlisted for GLOP, PDLP, HiGHS and SCIP
a model with only integer variables is shortlisted for HiGHS, SCIP and CP-SAT
each solver on a shortlist solves the model to OPTIMAL
a model with integer and continuous variables is shortlisted for HiGHS and SCIP only
an LP whose caller needs dual values is shortlisted for GLOP, PDLP and HiGHS
a model with an integer variable whose caller needs dual values gets an empty shortlist

origin.section: Five Solvers Are Built Into the pip Package, and Gurobi Needs Its Own Library and License

concepts: CP-SAT rounds continuous variables and still reports OPTIMAL, so it gets all-integer models only
GLOP and PDLP refuse integer variables, and only GLOP, PDLP and HiGHS return LP duals
